question: Which newspaper edited by Bal Gangadhar Tilak, was one of the strongest critics of the British rule?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kesari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kesari newspaper published in the Marathi language **is one of the strongest critics of British rule. 
 
• **Kesari **was founded by nationalist leader **Lokmanya** **Bal Gangadhar Tilak on 4 Januray 1881.**
 
• The newspaper was actively used as the **voice of the Indian National freedom movement**.
 
• In **1897 Bal Gangadhar Tilak **was charged by the British government for **his critical views in the newspaper against the government. ​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Lokmanya B. G. Tilak started two newspapers **Kesari in Marathi language and Maratha in English language**.
 
• Many prominent freedom fighters became editors of these newspapers, like **Vishnushastri Chiplunkar, and Gopal Ganesh Agarkar.**
 
• **Amrita Bazar Patrika** was started by** Sisir Ghosh and Moti Lal Ghosh in 1868.**
 
• **The Tribune is an Indian English-language **daily newspaper **founded in 1881 by Sardar Dyal Singh.**
 
• **The Hindu **is an English daily newspaper founded by **G Subramanyam Iyer in 1878**.
